## What is wrong

`tests/integration/test_similar_tickets_scale.py`, in
`test_the_cold_catch_up_cost_at_that_scale_is_emitted_as_a_number`, ends with:

```python
assert isinstance(p95, float)
assert p95 > 0.0
```

Any wall-clock sample satisfies both unconditionally. A duration measured with a
monotonic clock is a float, and it is positive. No behaviour of the code under test
makes that pair fail.

## Correcting this ticket's own premise

The ticket as filed said the test cannot catch "a catch-up that silently indexes
nothing". Re-reading the body shows that is wrong. The loop already asserts
`result["indexed"] >= MIN_TICKETS` on every iteration, so a rebuild that indexed
nothing already fails the test today.

The vacuity is confined to the trailing pair, and the fix is correspondingly narrow:
the test is one real counted invariant plus two assertions that assert nothing.

## What replaces the vacuous pair

A wall-clock ceiling is the obvious candidate and is the wrong one. `47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88`
replaced exactly such a budget with `WARM_TO_COLD_RATIO` before this file landed, after its planned 500 ms criterion measured 107 ms on the development host and 545 ms on `macos-latest` (47c8 comment "Why the warm-path criterion changed"). The file has a single commit, `c43d9336262`, so it never carried the budget itself. The replacement is a counted
invariant instead, in the same spirit as `WARM_TO_COLD_RATIO`:

**A cold rebuild leaves nothing for the next catch-up to write.** After the final
rebuild, the test runs `catch_up` once more on the same connection and asserts the
result reports `indexed == 0` and `dropped == 0` over a `scanned` count of at least
`MIN_TICKETS`.

This is not idempotence of work, it is idempotence of effect, and the distinction is
the point. The warm-query test's docstring (`test_similar_tickets_scale.py:156-157`) records that the run after any indexing run re-hashes
the directories it just indexed, because re-indexing moves their mtimes. So the second
catch-up does real work; what it must not do is write. The assertion fails if the
rebuild stored a hash that does not match what re-hashing produces, if it indexed only
part of the store while still clearing `MIN_TICKETS`, or if ticket reduction is not
deterministic across two reads of the same directory. None of those is reachable by the
existing `indexed >= MIN_TICKETS` check, and none depends on how fast the host is.

The cost figure keeps being printed. It is a measurement the ADR cites and removing it
would lose that; it simply stops being dressed as an assertion.

## Sweep for the same shape

Every `assert` in the file was read. The pair at the end of this one test is the only
occurrence of an assertion that no behaviour of the code under test can falsify. Two
that look thin on a first pass are not: `assert results` can fail, because
`find_similar` returns `[]` when nothing matches, and `assert not present` can fail,
because `monkeypatch.delenv` leaves the name set when the variable was not deleted. The
change names this sweep and its result so the question is not reopened.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `assert isinstance(p95, float)` and `assert p95 > 0.0` are gone from the file. Verified by grepping the file for `isinstance(p95`.
- [x] The test runs `catch_up` once more after the final rebuild and asserts the result reports `indexed == 0`. Verified by reading the test body.
- [x] That same follow-up assertion also covers `dropped == 0`. Verified by reading the test body.
- [x] That same follow-up assertion also covers `scanned >= MIN_TICKETS`, so a catch-up that scanned an empty store cannot satisfy the other two. Verified by reading the test body.
- [x] A test demonstrates the new invariant fails when it is violated, by setting one stored `dirstate` row's `dir_mtime_ns` stale AND its `dir_hash` wrong -- both are required, because `_changed` (`catchup.py:163`) skips any directory whose stored mtime still matches the live mtime before the hash is ever read, so a hash-only corruption would report `indexed == 0` -- then asserting the follow-up catch-up reports `indexed > 0`. Verified by that test.
- [x] No assertion added by this change compares a duration against a fixed millisecond constant. Verified by grepping the diff for a numeric literal in a comparison against a `_ms` name.
- [x] The cold-cost figure is still printed through `capsys.disabled()`. Verified by reading the test body.
- [x] The test's name states the property it now asserts rather than that it emits a number. Verified by reading the name.
- [x] The sweep result is recorded in the test module's docstring, naming the two assertions examined and kept. Verified by reading the docstring.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0. Verified by running it.

## Provenance

Raised as an advisory, non-blocking finding by the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on change
3211 patchset 2. No change was made under `47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88` because it was the
keystone blocking three tickets and resetting its gates for a non-blocking test issue
was not worth the round trip. The emission is kept because the number it prints is one the binding design record now
cites. `docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md:231` records a cold catch-up p95 of
12,455 ms at n=5, over the synthetic 10,000-ticket store named at `:226`, and that is
this test's sample. A figure that enters the ADR should come from something that can
fail if the figure is wrong, which is precisely what this ticket adds; deleting the
print instead would leave the ADR's number with no producer at all.
